title: Pat McAfee and crew roast ESPN's Heather Dinich for absurd College Football Playoff metrics
text:
McAfee's show took their own employer to task after the latest college football playoff rankings sparked SEC bias debate

CFP Committee & ESPN's Paul Finebaum SLANDER Indiana As SEC Bias Questions MOUNT | Don't @ Me w/ Dan Dakich

Fans and coaches across college football are erupting over a Top 25 stacked with 6-4 SEC teams and two-loss Alabama getting propped up while Indiana gets penalized.

A lot has been made about the latest College Football Playoff rankings, though when is that ever not the case?

I'm not here to discuss whether or not the powers that be are in cahoots with any one conference or if ESPN is exhibiting " SEC bias," but there seems to be a lot of chatter on social media, almost too much to ignore.

Most of this stems from The Worldwide Leader's wrap-up coverage from Tuesday night's CFP rankings reveal, during which ESPN's Heather Dinich unveiled a new metric called "Strength of Conference."

ESPN'S HEATHER DINICH DESTROYED BY CFB FANS OVER MYSTERY PLAYOFF RANKING METRIC, UCLA CHEERLEADERS & TARPS OFF

ESPN College Football Playoff Insider and reporter Heather Dinich during the 2024 Big Ten Media Days on July 25, 2024, at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis, Ind. (Icon Sportswire via Getty Images)

Dinich took plenty of heat for this, most of which came from fans online, but one prominent voice that works for the very same network may have just fired off a shot inside the ESPN tent.

Pat McAfee had Reece Davis on to make sense of what many are calling the most confusing CFP rankings in the history of the sport, and after Davis exited stage right, the boys took their own employer to task.

"It is hard not to just be like, 'there's a lot of SEC representation in there,'" McAfee said.

He also pointed out that there are plenty of SEC athletic directors who are on the CFP selection committee, and that Mark Dantonio might need to start "swinging a bit bigger fist."

NEW COLLEGE FOOTBALL PLAYOFF POLL PROVES THE SELECTION COMMITTEE IS JUST MAKING IT UP AS THEY GO

That's when Ty Schmitt, one of McAfee's crew members, dropped the bomb, referring to Dinich as a "turncoat."

Pat McAfee on the Pat McAfee Show set at the Super Bowl LX media center at the Moscone Center. (Kirby Lee/Imagn Images)

McAfee let out a sarcastic "no," before a voice off camera accused her of "making up new metrics."

"She couldn't explain it worth a damn," Schmitt said.

Obviously, the ribbing is mostly tongue-in-cheek from McAfee and crew, and if Dinich were on set with them, they’d be dishing it out right to her face.

I don't think there's anything nefarious going on here, but it is funny to see even people within the ESPN umbrella pushing the narrative that the CFP committee is compromised.

I wonder if Pat will be receiving a call from some of the higher-ups telling him to tone it down?

I digress.

Pat McAfee and the ESPN "College GameDay" crew appear on set in front of a crowd of college football fans. (Roger Wimmer/ISI Photos/ISI Photos via Getty Images)

Again, I'm not here to make a stink of the CFP rankings. I'll leave that to guys like Ian Miller (also, my Florida Gators are part of the problem as a ranked four-loss team, so I must recuse myself).

Suffice to say, we have a few weeks left until these rankings are actually final, so if I were you all, I'd save my breath until things are written in stone.

But then again, where's the fun in that?

Austin Perry is a writer for OutKick.
